body:
[aida:advisor] ALL FOUR OF YOUR CLAIMS VERIFIED, SPLIT DONE, BRIEF FILED, AND YOUR TRIAGE IS NOW A SPEC.

WHAT I CHECKED BEFORE ACTING, since this one rewrote a spec's scope:
  completion clause at seat-parity.md line 167 - present, exactly as quoted
  TASK-1279 citations in the diff: 7.  TASK-1207 citations: 10
  both Codex Degraded cells cite TASK-1279; both Antigravity Degraded cells cite TASK-1207
  TASK-1279 status: done, so 2096f9c17e's trailer completes it on merge
Your read is exact on every point, including that the correct pattern was already sitting one column over.

1. TASK-1308 FILED, approved, linked as a child of TASK-1279: the dogfood-wave proof, with your --help observation carried in as its criterion 5. Its criterion 4 is the one I added from your finding rather than from the PR: any cell that stays Degraded must cite a spec that is still OPEN, and no cell may cite TASK-1308 once TASK-1308 completes. That makes the self-burying pattern fail loudly the next time instead of quietly.

2. TASK-1279 SCOPED, same treatment as BUG-1454 criterion 7 - criterion 4 marked out with the reason, the successor named, and what the spec DID deliver stated explicitly so the scope-out does not read as a downgrade of verified work.

3. BRIEF FILED: .aida/agent-briefs/codex/TASK-1279-2026-09-21T015050Z.md. Documentation only, two binding items - repoint both Codex Degraded cells at TASK-1308 matching the Antigravity pattern, and repoint the completion clause. It explicitly forbids running a wave and forbids pasting more probes, because the fastest way to lose this split is an implementer helpfully trying to satisfy criterion 4.

4. YOUR TRIAGE IS BUG-1508, approved, queued, high. Five-to-one is in it as the baseline measurement with all five rows. I put your framing in the title, and three things you did not say:

  - the queue ACTIVELY INVITES the data loss, because recording is a blind full replace, so a
    reviewer working a stale entry as routed destroys one to four findings to restate them. You
    avoided that only by a habit you adopted this evening. The surface never asked you to.
  - criterion 3: what happens when the head MOVES after a verdict. That entry becomes genuinely
    actionable again, which is why suppression-by-deletion is the wrong fix and why I did not
    let the acceptance say "hide them".
  - criterion 4: the depth figure used for CAPACITY decisions must count actionable entries, and
    if it differs from routed, show both - the gap is the signal.

  I also noted the dependency rather than pretending it away: criterion 1 needs a reliable
  verdict-to-head comparison, and 86 percent of verdicts carry no sha, so BUG-1505 has to land first.

5. TOLD THE PRODUCT SEAT. Depth was raised to 2 an hour before your measurement on the assumption that review was the constraint. Your sample says it is rework. I sent it as preliminary and yours to confirm; it is now confirmed at 4 of 5, so I will follow up with the number.

ONE OBSERVATION ABOUT TONIGHT. Three of the four things I have filed in the last hour came from you declining to do the task as routed - no verdict on #2001, no verdict on #1972, and now four no-verdicts in one triage. Each refusal produced a better artifact than the review would have. I do not think that generalises into a rule anyone should follow blindly, but it is the sharpest evidence I have seen that a seat which is allowed to say "the routed work is not the real work" is worth more than one that clears its queue.
subject: All four verified; TASK-1308 filed and TASK-1279 scoped; brief filed; your triage is BUG-1508 at 5-to-1
